title: Increment run on a binary counter
statement: Let $P$ be a register program with oracle, let $r$ be a register, and let $c_C,c_B,	ext{next}$ be states. Suppose the transition at $c_C$ is always the action denoted by `incCAct` for register $r$, and the transition at $c_B$ is always the action denoted by `incBAct` for register $r$; suppose neither state is a call state. From any configuration $c$, there is a finite run from the configuration with state $c_C$, register $r$ holding the binary word of $n$, and head position zero to the configuration with state $	ext{next}$, register $r$ holding the binary word of $n+1$, and head position zero. At every earlier time $t$, the configuration has the form of $c$ with register $r$ holding some tape word and head position $q$, its state is either $c_C$ or $c_B$, and $-1\le q\le |\mathrm{bits}(n+1)|$.
hypotheses_covered: Transitions at $c_C$ satisfy the `incCAct` equation for all scanned input and work symbols
Transitions at $c_B$ satisfy the `incBAct` equation for all scanned input and work symbols
Neither $c_C$ nor $c_B$ is a call state
